 Judgment
These appeals are against the judgment and award dated 26.04.2019 in MVC No.319/2017 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raichur (for short, 'the Tribunal').
The claimants' appeal is in MFA No.200290/2020, and the Insurer's appeal is in MFA No.201770/2019.

The claim petition in MVC No.319/2017 is filed by the wife, minor children and parents of the deceased Sri Basavareddy alias Basavaraj, and the Tribunal has allowed this petition awarding a total compensation of Rs.16,31,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum directing the Insurer to pay the compensation.

2. If the claimants seek enhancement of compensation in their appeal, the Insurer disputes the NC:
2023:KHC-K:1300-DB liability essentially reiterating its defense that the deceased is the owner of the insured vehicle and his legal heirs cannot sustain a claim against the Insurer who has insured the vehicle to indemnify.

The insurance policy is marked as Ex.R-2, and it is seen from this policy that an additional premium is received for Personal Accident [PA] claim coverage to the owner subject to a maximum of Rs.2,00,000/-.
The terms of this policy are not disputed.

Therefore, the question for consideration is whether the Tribunal is justified in calling upon the Insurer to pay the compensation in a sum of Rs.16,31,000/- or should the Insurer's liability to be confined to a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- because of this endorsement.

This Court, depending on the answer to this question,
will have to consider whether there should be enhancement in the compensation as sought for by the claimants in their appeal.

3. It is undisputed that the deceased Sri Basavareddy alias Basavaraj is the owner of the tempo traveller bearing Reg.No.KA-36/A-671, and he had NC: 2023:KHC-K:1300-DB insured this vehicle with the Insurer under the policy dated 17.02.2011 which was in force as of the date of the accident i.e., 10.07.2011.
The first respondent was driving the vehicle at the time of the accident, and because of the injuries suffered in this accident the deceased Sri Basavareddy alias Basavaraj has died on the spot.

The Insurer's defense must necessarily be considered in the light of these circumstances and the settled law that contract of insurance is an indemnity contract to indemnify the insured against the third party claimants or to pay the amount as may be contractually agreed.

A useful reference in this regard could be made to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramkhiladi and another vs. United India Insurance Company and another reported in (2020) 2 SCC 550.
4.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi and another vs. United India Insurance Company and another reported in (2020) 2 SCC 550
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has overlooked both the circumstances of the case and the settled position.

Of course, the Tribunal has reasoned that because a premium is collected both for covering the owner and the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1300-DB driver, the insurer must be made liable, but this Court must observe that in the absence of any evidence in this regard by the claimants and the evidence of the Insurer's witness that in a Package Policy the liability to the Insured would only be of the extent of the endorsement, this Court is not persuaded to opine that the liability can be fastened on the Insurer beyond Rs.2,00,000/-, and the question for consideration is answered accordingly and the Insurer's liability to the claimants is confined to a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-.
Further, the Insurer, in the circumstances of the case where even the admitted liability is not tendered, must be called upon to pay the said interest at the rate of 9% per annum.

With the question being answered as aforesaid,
the claimants' appeal will not survive.
